# Sync Austin permit use changes to Google Sheets with Apify

For analysts tracking changes in how commercial properties may be used, this workflow turns Austin permit descriptions into a Google Sheet. It uses Record Foundry’s [Austin commercial use-change API](https://apify.com/recordfoundry/austin-commercial-use-changes).

## How it works

Each run checks the last 14 completed UTC dates. Matching permits become rows with the previous use, planned use, exact supporting wording, original description, official record link, and source timestamps. The `permitKey` column updates existing rows on repeat runs. Source text is written literally using Sheets’ RAW setting.

## Setup

Create a spreadsheet tab named `Permits` with the headers in the setup note. Enter its spreadsheet ID in **Set user configuration**. Connect an Apify HTTP Header Auth credential (`Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN`) and Google Sheets OAuth2. Run manually once; then enable the Monday 7 AM America/Chicago schedule if useful.

## Costs and coverage

The template is free. The API charges $1 per nonempty report; empty reports are free. Each request has a $1 charge limit. n8n hosting costs are separate. There are no automatic retries after an uncertain start.

Malformed reports fail visibly; valid empty reports write nothing. A permit describes planned work, not a confirmed business opening. Weekly overlapping windows can miss later revisions or records published after the window. Run sequentially: concurrent sheet writes can duplicate rows. The sheet retains earlier rows; it is not a deletion-synchronized archive.

## Spreadsheet setup

Create a tab named **Permits**. Paste this tab-separated header row into A1:

```text
permitKey	city	recordId	permitNumber	location	sourceIssueDate	sourceStatus	priorUses	plannedUses	evidenceQuotes	sourceDescription	sourceUrl	sourceUpdatedAt	collectedAt	reportStartDate	reportEndDate	schemaVersion	ruleVersion	sourceQuery
```

Enter the spreadsheet ID in **Set user configuration**. Attach Apify Header Auth and Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials. In the last node, match on **permitKey** and retain **Let n8n format / RAW**. Keep one execution at a time.

After an uncertain timeout, inspect the existing Apify run before retrying. A retry can create another charge.

## 1. Choose the destination

Set your Google spreadsheet ID, attach both credentials, and run manually first. The date step rejects the placeholder before starting a paid request.

Each run uses the last 14 completed UTC issue dates. Weekly windows overlap, but later revisions and records published after the window may be missed.

## 2. Fetch and validate the report

The Actor request has a $1 maximum charge and no automatic retry. After a timeout, inspect the existing Apify run before starting another.

Validation checks the requested dates, schema, official source, counts, duplicate IDs, and supporting quotes. A valid empty report produces no sheet rows; malformed data stops the workflow.

## 3. Update the review sheet

Match the single **permitKey** column. Keep **Let n8n format / RAW** so source descriptions remain literal text. Original wording, evidence quotes, official links and timestamps stay with each row.

Run sequentially to avoid concurrent duplicates. Previously written rows remain even if a source record later disappears or stops matching. Permits do not confirm a business opening or completed construction.
